categories.title: Conversation & creation
categories.description: Develop ideas, explore difficult topics, write, and analyse information together with AI.
categories.analogy: Think of a conversation partner, editor, and consultant in one interface.
categories.example: “Help me plan a charity event and write an invitation to potential partners.”

categories.title: Research & knowledge synthesis
categories.description: Find connections between your documents, notes, and reports, then draw conclusions from them.
categories.analogy: Think of an assistant who has read your folder of documents and helps you find what matters.
categories.example: “Compare these three reports: summarise their themes, shared conclusions, and differences. Cite the relevant passages and flag missing evidence.”

categories.title: Work inside a project
categories.description: Ask AI to explore project files, change code, run commands, and check the result.
categories.analogy: Think of a development partner: give it a specific task and review the work.
categories.example: “Add a new page to this learning website and check that the navigation works.”

categories.title: Connect external tools
categories.description: Use search, files, email, calendars, or other services through AI when the relevant integrations and permissions are available.
categories.analogy: Think of an assistant you can authorise to perform specific actions on your behalf.
categories.example: “Find the email with the event programme and help me add a meeting to my calendar,” if supported.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.summary: Get help with writing, ideas, learning, and analysing your data.
tools.analogy: A versatile assistant for intellectual tasks, from an early idea to data analysis.
tools.description: Describe a problem in everyday language, read the response, clarify your requirements, and refine the result together.
tools.example: For a charity event, ask for a plan, analyse your expense spreadsheet, draft a partner email, or develop a visual concept.
capabilities: Search for information and research topics
Use additional tools available in your mode
tools.limitation: Check facts even when the answer sounds convincing. Features and limits depend on your plan and available mode.

tools.name: Gemini
tools.summary: Combine conversation, research, and supported Google services.
tools.analogy: A digital assistant for conversation, research, and work within the Google ecosystem.
tools.description: Use Google's assistant, based on the Gemini model family, for learning, brainstorming, research, analysing materials, and creating content.
tools.example: Ask for an explanation of a difficult topic, current sources for research, or a presentation outline. Use supported Google services when the necessary integrations are enabled.
capabilities: Search for information and explore topics
Work with text, images, and files
Try voice interaction and features available in your version
tools.limitation: An integration does not automatically grant access to every file, email, or calendar. Check account settings, permissions, and supported features.

tools.name: Claude
tools.summary: Edit writing, analyse documents, and examine complex arguments.
tools.analogy: An attentive editor and analyst: ask it to examine reasoning as well as shorten a document.
tools.description: Work with language, analysis, reasoning, and code using Anthropic's Claude assistant.
tools.example: Upload a long report and ask it to find contradictions, separate facts from assumptions, or compare authors' positions. Verify the conclusions against the passages.
capabilities: Solve programming tasks using available features
tools.limitation: Good analysis does not guarantee factual accuracy. Check sources and search availability when you need current information.

tools.name: NotebookLM
tools.summary: Add documents to get answers, comparisons, and learning materials grounded in them.
tools.analogy: A research assistant for a specific folder of sources, rather than a general conversation.
tools.description: Add sources to Google's NotebookLM, ask questions, analyse the content, and create study materials. Distinguish this source-focused product from the general Gemini chat.
tools.example: Add notes, research papers, and a presentation. Compare definitions, prepare self-test questions, or generate an Audio Overview.
capabilities: Ask questions grounded in your sources
Generate Audio Overviews and other supported formats
tools.limitation: Source completeness, currency, and consistency shape the answer. Open citations and check what they actually support.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.summary: Delegate code exploration, file changes, and checks in your project.
tools.analogy: A development partner that can explain code, edit files, and check the work.
tools.description: Give Claude Code a sequence of tasks in a software project: explore code, edit files, run commands, and verify the result.
tools.example: Ask it to explore a learning website, add a page, or investigate an error. Review the changes and check results.
capabilities: Work with Git and configured tools
tools.limitation: Control permissions, review changes, and verify results. Edits and commands can have unintended effects.

tools.name: Codex
tools.summary: Describe a task and get an implemented change, checks, and an explanation.
tools.analogy: An assistant that carries out technical tasks in your project for you to review.
tools.description: Use OpenAI Codex to explore a codebase, implement changes, fix bugs, and run checks. Choose an available local, editor, or cloud environment.
tools.example: Ask for a feature, tests, and an explanation. Review the changed files and confirm your requirements were met.
capabilities: Analyse changes and prepare them for review
Delegate sequences of actions within the available environment
tools.limitation: Review the result and grant access only to files, commands, and external systems needed for the task.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.summary: Get suggestions in your editor, discuss code, and delegate changes to an agent.
tools.analogy: A partner in your editor, from suggesting the next line to tackling a repository task.
tools.description: Use GitHub Copilot in supported editors and on GitHub. Complete code, ask questions in chat, and use agent capabilities available in your plan and environment.
tools.example: Ask it to explain an unfamiliar function, propose tests, and implement a small change. Review the diff and run checks.
capabilities: Discuss code and errors in chat
Delegate changes in supported agent environments
tools.limitation: Feature availability depends on your plan, editor, and organisation policies. Verify code, dependencies, and test results; a suggestion does not guarantee correctness.
tools.object: Code, open files, and repository context
tools.result: Suggestions, explanations, tests, and code changes
